school_ability: May the Spirits Show the Path

answers.stand_out: Asahi tends to be comfortable with conflict and with tension, holding differing perspectives simultaneously.

answers.social_giri: Tonbo Unkei, her daimyō, wants her to present the Dragonfly clan as an independent entity, not merely a vassal of the Dragon clan.

answers.social_ninjo: She longs to understand the true nature of her visions, and what purpose they are to serve.

answers.clan_relations: She serves her clan loyally, but wonders if they will support her should her visions cause problems for them.

answers.bushido: She believes in bushidō, but her visions give her an element of fatalism that she has not been able to square with the demands of virtue.

answers.success: Visions of prosperity comingled with ruin came to her during negotiations at Still Water Temple. She urged the negotiator to accept the treaty, but to prepare contingencies. When mercenaries attacked, the clan was prepared; but as a result her visions are sometimes viewed with more certainty than she is comfortable ascribing to them.

answers.difficulty: She has only traveled to another clan's territories three times; each time, she just...arrived. She had no memory of the journey after leaving her home territory. Her traveling companions did not recognize anything different about her. She does not know the cause, but it troubles her.

answers.calms: There is nothing quite like the practice of rock gardening to help center yourself.

answers.worries: Sometimes, the blanket wraps too tight and she awakens in terror; her fear of being trapped in a small space induces panic and terror.

answers.most_learn:
Tonbo Umeko is a minor courtier from a cadet branch of the Tonbo family who found her calling as a matchmaker. While others saw only Asahi's visions, Umeko taught her to also observe the small human details—a hesitation before speaking, the way someone holds their hands, the subtle shift in a room's atmosphere.

Umeko treats Asahi with the fond exasperation of an older sister, simultaneously proud of her accomplishments and worried about her melancholic tendencies. She brings Asahi gossip from other courts, practical gifts, and unsolicited romantic advice (which Asahi politely ignores).

answers.first_sight: She speaks so quietly that people must lean in to hear her, and she never raises her voice, even in crisis.

answers.stress: She is silent but the tears flow easily, and her shoulders shudder.

answers.relations:
Mirumoto Takeshi: Dragon clan liason; he is Asahi's main contact, but it's always a strictly business relationship.

Yogo Ren: A Scorpion clan courtier who passes through often; they are on friendly terms.

Monks of the Still Water Temple: She has a delicate relationship with them; her reputation is good, but she is not a monk and she tries to maintain a formal distinction.

answers.parents_pov: Asahi-sama is no longer truly our daughter - she belongs to the kami and the visions now. We speak to her with the same formality we would use with any holy person. When she visits, we treat her as an honored guest.

answers.heritage_name: Tonbo Asahi (the Elder) was a celebrated poet and lady-in-waiting at the Imperial Court 120 years ago. Her waka moved even the Emperor to tears. When she bore a child that same winter, officially fathered by a minor courtier who conveniently died soon after, everyone at court knew the truth but it was never spoken directly. The child was quietly sent to the Dragonfly Clan, and Tonbo Asahi (the Elder) took the tonsure and became a nun. Her poetry scrolls remain treasured, but her name is mentioned only with careful ambiguity.

answers.death: She never saw it coming, and the surprise delighted her.
